answer: Submissions that land within 191 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The terrace detector writes to tide, and pearl reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 237 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 5 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
